newsitem.title: USA: Greyhound January passenger tickets up.
newsitem.headline: Greyhound January passenger tickets up.

text.p: Greyhound Lines Inc said Wednesday it had a gain of 14.5 percent in passenger ticket sales for January, over the same month last year, at its top 198 electronic reporting locations.

"Our January traffic rose because of strong sales of our advance-purchase discount fares, continued improvement in the efficiency of our operations, and an increase in advertising expenditures," Steven Korby, executive vice president and chief financial officer, said in a statement released by the company.
Sales last January were reduced by severe winter weather in the Northeast, he added.
Passengers carried during the month increased 16.1 percent, the company said.
The yield, or sales per passenger mile, declined 2.7 percent to $0.897 cents, reflecting the impact of promotional pricing and an increase in long haul travel, the company said.
